title: Resource locks: CanNotDelete and ReadOnly
learningObjective: Apply the right lock at the right scope, predict which operations it blocks (including side effects of ReadOnly), and remove or work around locks safely.
foundation: A resource lock is a safety catch that stops important resources from being deleted or changed by accident, even by administrators.
There are two kinds. CanNotDelete (shown as 'Delete' in the portal): people can still read and change the resource but cannot delete it. ReadOnly: people can only read it; no changes and no deletes.
You can lock a subscription, a resource group or a single resource. A lock on a resource group protects everything inside it.
To change or delete a locked resource, someone with permission must remove the lock first. That extra step is the point.
engineer: Locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager on control-plane requests sent to management.azure.com. CanNotDelete blocks DELETE. ReadOnly blocks PUT, PATCH, DELETE and POST, so it behaves like the Reader role for everyone.

Locks apply to every user and role, including Owner. Creating or deleting locks requires Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* (for example Owner or User Access Administrator). Contributor cannot manage locks.
Locks are inherited: a lock on a subscription or resource group applies to all resources below it, and the most restrictive lock in effect wins. Locks cannot be applied at management group scope.
Deleting a resource group or subscription fails if any resource inside it is locked, because ARM would have to delete the locked resource.

ReadOnly has side effects on POST actions. On a storage account it prevents listing the account keys, so the portal cannot fall back to key-based data access. On a resource group containing a VM it prevents starting or restarting the VM. On an App Service it stops Visual Studio Server Explorer from showing the app's files, because that interaction needs write access.

Data-plane operations are not affected: CanNotDelete on a storage account does not stop someone deleting blobs or files with data-plane permissions, and it does not stop a SQL user dropping tables. Use soft delete, versioning or immutability for data.

A CanNotDelete lock on a resource group can stop services from cleaning up their own resources, for example Azure Backup deleting restore point collections. Lock the specific resource instead when that matters.

example.title: Protecting shared networking
body: The hub VNet, VPN gateway and Azure Firewall live in rg-connectivity. The platform team applies CanNotDelete to rg-connectivity, so network engineers can still update routes and rules but nobody can delete the gateway by mistake.

They do not use ReadOnly on the resource group: it would block legitimate changes and POST operations such as resetting the gateway. A ReadOnly lock is reserved for a production storage account's configuration during an audit freeze, with clients using Entra ID authentication, because listing keys stops working.

prerequisites: Target subscription, resource group or resource ID
permissions: Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* (Owner, User Access Administrator, or a custom role)
limits: Scopes: subscription, resource group or resource (not management group)
portal: Open the subscription, resource group or resource > Settings > Locks > Add.
Enter a name, choose Lock type Delete (CanNotDelete) or Read-only, and add notes explaining why.
To remove: Locks > Delete on the lock (requires locks/* permission), perform the change, then re-create the lock.
configuration.cli:
az lock create --name lk-rg-prod --lock-type CanNotDelete --resource-group rg-prod --notes "Protect production"
az lock create --name lk-st1 --lock-type ReadOnly --resource-group rg-prod \
  --resource-name st1 --resource-type Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts
az lock list --resource-group rg-prod -o table
az lock delete --name lk-rg-prod --resource-group rg-prod
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceLock -LockName lk-rg-prod -LockLevel CanNotDelete -ResourceGroupName rg-prod -LockNotes 'Protect production'
New-AzResourceLock -LockName lk-st1 -LockLevel ReadOnly -ResourceGroupName rg-prod `
  -ResourceName st1 -ResourceType Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts
Get-AzResourceLock -ResourceGroupName rg-prod
Remove-AzResourceLock -LockName lk-rg-prod -ResourceGroupName rg-prod

lab.objective: Show what each lock level blocks, including inherited locks, child locks and ReadOnly side effects.
steps: Add CanNotDelete on rg-prod. Update vm1 (succeeds), then delete vm1 (blocked by an inherited lock).
Use the scenario 'Delete RG that contains a locked resource' and send it. The delete fails because of the child lock.
Use the scenario 'ReadOnly lock vs. listing storage keys'. The POST listKeys action is blocked.
Send 'Read vm1' (GET) with a ReadOnly lock in place. Reads still succeed.
expected: RG deletion blocked by a lock inside it
POST blocked by ReadOnly; GET allowed

validation.text: A delete was blocked by a lock
Resource group deletion was blocked by a lock on a resource inside it
A POST action was blocked by a ReadOnly lock

failureScenarios: Expecting Owner to bypass a lock
Expecting CanNotDelete to protect blob data
Putting ReadOnly on a resource group and breaking VM start/stop automation
lab.cost: None. Locks are free; the simulation runs in the browser.

troubleshooting.symptom: Owner gets ScopeLocked when deleting a resource.
troubleshooting.cause: A CanNotDelete or ReadOnly lock on the resource, its resource group or its subscription.
troubleshooting.fix: az lock list --resource-group <rg> (inherited locks show their scope); remove the lock if the change is approved.

troubleshooting.symptom: Resource group deletion fails although the group itself has no lock.
troubleshooting.cause: A resource inside the group is locked.
troubleshooting.fix: Find and remove the lock on the child resource first.

troubleshooting.symptom: Portal shows 'You do not have permissions to list the data using your user account' on a storage account.
troubleshooting.cause: A ReadOnly lock blocks the listKeys POST, so key-based access fails.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Entra ID authentication with a Storage Blob Data role, or replace ReadOnly with CanNotDelete.

troubleshooting.symptom: Automation cannot start VMs in the morning.
troubleshooting.cause: ReadOnly lock on the resource group blocks POST start actions.
troubleshooting.fix: Use CanNotDelete instead, or lock individual resources.

comparisons.difference: RBAC grants permissions per principal; locks restrict operations for all principals regardless of role.
DenyAction can block delete actions based on resource properties across a scope (for example by tag), whereas a lock targets one specific scope.
Deployment stacks can create deny assignments that stop changes to the resources the stack manages, with excluded principals; locks have no exclusions.
EC2 termination protection and CloudFormation stack termination protection are per-resource flags; Azure locks are separate inherited objects at subscription/RG/resource scope.

misconceptions.myth: Owners are not affected by locks.
misconceptions.reality: Locks apply to everyone. An Owner can remove the lock, but must do so first.

misconceptions.myth: ReadOnly only blocks edits in the portal.
misconceptions.reality: It blocks every write and POST on the control plane, including listing storage keys and starting VMs.

misconceptions.myth: CanNotDelete on a storage account protects the data in it.
misconceptions.reality: Locks do not apply to data-plane operations such as deleting blobs.

misconceptions.myth: You can lock a management group.
misconceptions.reality: Locks apply at subscription, resource group or resource scope.

architectureDecisions: Use CanNotDelete on production and shared-infrastructure resource groups as a default safety net.
Reserve ReadOnly for short freezes or rarely changed resources, after checking POST-based side effects.
Manage locks as code (Bicep) alongside the resources they protect so they are not forgotten.
Combine locks with soft delete, backups and RBAC; locks do not protect data or configuration changes made by authorized users.

walkthrough.subtitle: Stop important resources being deleted or changed by accident, even by Owners.

steps.label: Oops
steps.title: An Owner deletes production by mistake
body: Owners can do anything, including deleting the wrong resource group. RBAC alone cannot stop someone who has the rights.

steps.label: Two locks
steps.title: Two kinds of lock
body: CanNotDelete (shown as Delete in the portal): people can read and change the resource, but not delete it. ReadOnly: people can read it but not change or delete it.
Locks apply to everyone, including Owners. To delete, someone must first remove the lock, which needs Owner or User Access Administrator.

steps.label: Inheritance
steps.title: Lock a resource group, protect everything in it
body: A lock on a subscription or resource group applies to every resource inside, including ones created later. The most restrictive lock wins.

steps.label: Side effects
steps.title: Case: ReadOnly breaks more than you expect
body: Some 'read' actions are really POST requests. A ReadOnly lock on a storage account blocks listing its access keys, so apps and the portal cannot get the keys. It also stops a VM from being started or resized.

callout.text: ReadOnly can break normal operations. CanNotDelete is the usual choice for production.

handsOn.title: Lock a resource group and watch a delete fail
handsOn.cost: Free. The storage account costs cents per month if left empty; you delete it at the end.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Create a storage account in rg-az104-lab (Standard, LRS) if you do not have one. Name it st<yourinitials><number>.
Open rg-az104-lab > Settings > Locks > + Add. Name: no-delete, lock type: Delete. OK.
steps.see: The lock listed with type Delete.

steps.do: Open the storage account and select Delete.
steps.see: An error that the resource is locked and cannot be deleted.

steps.do: Back on rg-az104-lab > Locks, edit the lock and change its type to Read-only. Save.
Open the storage account > Security + networking > Access keys and select Show.
steps.see: An error, or the keys do not load. Listing keys is blocked by the ReadOnly lock.

steps.do: Try to add a tag to the storage account.
steps.see: Saving fails: the lock prevents changes.
The Locks page is empty again.

check: You saw a delete blocked and a key listing blocked.
cleanup: Make sure the lock is deleted first.
When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
